title: Current standards, codification, packaging, and deployment for a skill suite

tldr.content: Use a two-layer suite: standards-compliant `SKILL.md` directories for portability, plus explicit host adapters and a machine-readable suite manifest for permissions, dependencies, tests, provenance, and deployment. Codify behavior with schemas, semantic validators, contract fixtures, adversarial tests, and dated refresh checks. A deterministic immutable archive with digest, signature, provenance, and SBOM is a defensible release policy, followed by host-specific staged deployment. Agent Skills metadata is not a security boundary. [ref-agent-spec][ref-slsa-verify][ref-nist-measure]

executiveSummary.content:
The Agent Skills standard defines the smallest portable unit: a directory with `SKILL.md`, required `name` and `description`, and optional resources. OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex add different discovery roots, invocation controls, permission models, plugin formats, and deployment behavior, so operational semantics should not be forced into the portable file. [ref-agent-spec][ref-opencode][ref-claude-skills][ref-codex-skills]

```text
canonical sources -> portable SKILL.md tree -> suite manifest/adapters
       -> schemas + semantic validators + contract/eval corpus
       -> deterministic archive -> digest/signature/provenance/SBOM
       -> verify -> host-specific staging/canary -> telemetry -> rollback
```

The pinned repository evidence documents a substantial local contract-and-build system. The current evidence does not establish public publication, production trust anchors, deployment-like evaluation, production telemetry, or a real canary/rollback result. [ref-local-manifest][ref-local-registry][ref-local-pack][ref-local-evals][ref-local-readiness]

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported: The portable Agent Skills unit is a directory containing `SKILL.md`; standard frontmatter requires `name` and `description`, with optional `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, and experimental `allowed-tools`. [ref-agent-spec]

K2. supported: Discovery, precedence, invocation syntax, permission enforcement, dependency resolution, sandboxing, side effects, versioning, and distribution are not fully standardized across Agent Skills hosts. [ref-agent-integration][ref-opencode][ref-claude-skills][ref-codex-skills]

K3. partially-supported: The standard recommends progressive disclosure and focused `SKILL.md` files, with references, scripts, and assets loaded as needed; this is authoring guidance, not a universal host requirement. [ref-agent-spec][ref-agent-integration]

K4. partially-supported: For production assurance, the suite should supplement structural schemas with semantic invariants, behavioral evaluation, and runtime security and traceability controls; this is an operating model rather than a formal four-layer standard. [ref-json-schema][ref-nist-measure][ref-owasp-llm]

K5. partially-supported: The pinned repository evidence documents implementation and tests for 14 skills, per-skill adapters, schema registration and compatibility, digest-bound artifacts, deterministic bootstrap parity checks, evaluation fixtures, telemetry, and rollout controls; this is not proof of public release or deployment. [ref-local-manifest][ref-local-registry][ref-local-pack][ref-local-evals]

K6. partially-supported: The repository is locally well-specified and checked but lacks independently evidenced production deployment, trust anchors, production telemetry, representative deployment-like evaluation, and real canary/rollback results. [ref-local-readiness]

K7. partially-supported: A canonical deterministic versioned archive is a defensible suite release policy, with ecosystem-specific packages or plugins deriving from it where behavioral parity is required; the cited standards do not mandate this policy. [ref-codex-plugin][ref-npm-pack][ref-slsa-distribute]

K8. partially-supported: Release verification should bind the exact artifact digest to trusted signer/builder identity, source repository, build type, and expected parameters. Signatures and provenance provide supply-chain evidence, not proof of runtime safety. [ref-slsa-verify][ref-npm-trusted][ref-npm-provenance]

K9. partially-supported: A suite may publish an SPDX SBOM as an independently maintained inventory artifact alongside release metadata; this is a policy recommendation, not an SPDX mandate, and an SBOM is not proof that the suite is safe. [ref-spdx][ref-slsa-distribute]

K10. partially-supported: A recommended deployment control sequence is verification, staging, host-specific smoke tests, limited canarying, monitored redacted telemetry, and rollback to a previously verified artifact; this is proposed policy, not a universal requirement. [ref-slsa-verify][ref-github-immutable][ref-nist-measure]

K11. partially-supported: A dated compatibility matrix and recurring validator and activation-test refreshes are recommended operational controls for managing host and specification drift; they are not mandated by the cited sources. [ref-agent-integration][ref-nist-measure]

detailSections.content:
### Portable core

Each skill remains independently consumable:

```text
<skill-name>/
  SKILL.md
  references/
  scripts/
  assets/
```

Use standard frontmatter only in the portable variant. Require directory/name identity, concise trigger-oriented descriptions, explicit inputs/outputs, boundaries, failure states, side effects, and examples. Keep instructions focused and use shallow relative resource references. [ref-agent-spec]

### Suite contract

Put operational semantics in a versioned suite manifest and per-skill contracts. Declare supported hosts, capability prerequisites, permissions, side-effect class, input/output schemas, artifact ownership, dependency closure, evaluator IDs, content digest, license, and deprecation status. Keep authority, credentials, trust roots, publication, commits, execution, and hard resource ceilings host-owned. [ref-local-manifest][ref-local-registry]

### Assurance stack

This is a proposed operating model, not a standards taxonomy:

1. Validate frontmatter, names, resource containment, license metadata, and executable-file policy.
2. Validate manifests and per-skill data with JSON Schema 2020-12.
3. Run semantic validators for edges, authority, revision compatibility, paths, and dependency closure.
4. Run producer-consumer fixtures and deterministic behavioral evaluations.
5. Run adversarial tests for prompt injection, secret leakage, path traversal, symlinks, hostile scripts, network and credential access, excessive agency, resource exhaustion, MCP/native-command exposure, and approval bypass.
6. Record redacted evidence, digests, test corpus/version, and release identity. [ref-json-schema][ref-nist-measure][ref-owasp-llm][ref-local-evals]

### Host adapters

Publish one portable tree plus adapters, not divergent behavior:

| Host | Adapter boundary | Deployment form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode | discovery roots, skill permissions, collision diagnostics, reload behavior | `.agents/skills` or OpenCode tree |
| Claude Code | placement, precedence, invocation controls, plugin namespace | Claude tree or plugin |
| Codex | `.agents/skills` scope, `agents/openai.yaml`, invocation policy, tool dependencies | Codex/ChatGPT plugin or tree |
| MCP/native/IDE/managed | explicit connector, command, IDE, or administrator-policy adapter | host-native package |

Adapters report resolved path, version, digest, collision result, permission result, and reload result. [ref-opencode][ref-claude-skills][ref-codex-skills][ref-codex-plugin]

### Release and deployment

A deterministic `.tgz` or equivalent archive is a defensible canonical release policy when it fits the consumers. Publish a release index with suite version, source commit, artifact and manifest digests, host matrix, schema revisions, evaluation evidence, SBOM reference, and rollback predecessor. Prefer trusted OIDC publishing where supported and mirror identical bytes to an immutable release. OCI, signed ZIP/TAR, plugin marketplace, or vendored trees are valid alternatives when their governance and consumer model fit better. [ref-npm-pack][ref-slsa-distribute][ref-npm-trusted][ref-github-immutable]

Proposed installer policy: download without executing package code; verify digest, signature, provenance, SBOM, and source/builder expectations; reject unsafe archive paths and unexpected files; validate the manifest; install to a new staging directory; smoke-test each adapter; activate atomically; and retain a prior verified digest where rollback is supported. Add capability brokers, secret isolation, egress controls, sandbox profiles, dependency pinning, malware scanning, VEX handling, human approvals, kill switches, and offline rollback bundles according to the threat model. [ref-slsa-verify][ref-nist-measure][ref-owasp-llm]

### Currentness and observability

Record source URL, publisher, retrieval date, publication/version data, and the local validator derived from each external source. Maintain a compatibility matrix for Agent Skills, OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, JSON Schema, release tooling, and runtime prerequisites. A scheduled refresh is a recommended control: detect changed host docs/specs, rerun portability fixtures, and block or quarantine stale releases. Telemetry should include suite/skill version, manifest/content digests, host adapter, activation, policy decision, evaluator version, error class, and rollback state, with secrets and user content redacted. Shadow, blue/green, feature-flag, limited-canary, or manual-approval rollout are alternatives selected by blast radius and rollback capability. [ref-agent-integration][ref-nist-measure]

recommendation.content:
Recommend this target architecture:

1. Use the Agent Skills specification as the portable authoring contract and add a validator for every `SKILL.md`, directory identity, description quality, optional-field portability, resource references, and body size. [ref-agent-spec]
2. Keep root skill directories canonical. Generate bootstrap payloads, manifests, registries, and host packages from them, with generated parity and complete dependency closure as release gates. [ref-local-pack]
3. Make the suite manifest the operational contract. Add host matrix, semantic policy, side-effect class, dependency closure, evaluator IDs, schema revisions, content digests, license, and deprecation metadata; keep authority and security policy outside ordinary skill metadata. [ref-local-manifest][ref-local-registry]
4. Add semantic and interaction validators beside JSON Schema, frozen contract fixtures, deterministic evaluations, and adversarial tests. Require independent review for high-risk execution, browser, publication, MCP/native-command, and generated-code skills. [ref-json-schema][ref-nist-measure][ref-owasp-llm]
5. Adopt a deterministic archive per immutable version if it fits the consumers. Record version, source commit, and SHA-256 digest; publish an SPDX SBOM and SLSA/in-toto provenance; sign artifact and attestations; and use OIDC trusted publishing where supported. [ref-spdx][ref-slsa-distribute][ref-slsa-verify][ref-npm-trusted]
6. Provide thin installers/adapters for `.agents/skills`, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex/ChatGPT plugins, with explicit alternatives for MCP, native commands, IDE extensions, managed configuration, OCI, and marketplace deployment. [ref-opencode][ref-claude-skills][ref-codex-skills][ref-codex-plugin]
7. Use shadow, staging, blue/green, feature flag, limited canary, or manual approval based on blast radius. Verify locally and at the consumer; collect redacted telemetry; retain the last known-good digest where rollback is supported. [ref-slsa-verify][ref-github-immutable][ref-nist-measure]
8. Add a scheduled standards refresh and host compatibility job. Re-run validators and representative activation tests when external specs or host docs change. [ref-agent-integration][ref-nist-measure]

Proceed with standards-aligned authoring and constrained packaging. Defer broad public deployment or autonomous execution until external publication, signing/trust roots, independent validation, deployment-like evaluation, telemetry export, and rollback are demonstrated. [ref-local-readiness]

unverifiedClaims.content:
Decision-blocking: Agent Skills and host documentation can change; compatibility requires refresh and release gating.

Decision-blocking: this run did not publish to npm, GitHub immutable releases, a Codex/ChatGPT plugin directory, or a Claude Skills API, and did not verify a real signature, provenance statement, SBOM, or consumer installer replay.

Material risk: current bootstrap closure and documentation consistency require release-level confirmation; local repository URLs do not represent uncommitted changes.

Material risk: schemas, digests, signatures, provenance, SBOMs, deterministic packaging, and green local tests do not establish semantic correctness, absence of malicious instructions, sandbox safety, or autonomous-execution safety.

Material risk: host discovery, precedence, permission, invocation, plugin, and reload semantics differ. Portability requires host-specific smoke tests.

Context-dependent: npm, GitHub Releases, OCI, plugin marketplaces, internal archives, and vendored trees have different governance and consumer trade-offs.

Unverifiable in this run: whether the proposed adapter layout, package format, refresh cadence, or evaluation suite improves adoption, latency, cost, correctness, or user trust without deployment measurements.

processAppendix.content:
Triage: DEEP, hybrid. Five independent read-only tracks covered portable standards, host ecosystems, packaging/provenance, codification/evaluation, and the local suite.

Synthesis separated portable format, host integration, machine contracts, behavioral evidence, runtime security, and release/deployment. The standard was treated as an authoring/discovery contract, not a package manager or security boundary.

Challenge: the independent challenger upheld the portable-format and host-gap claims, but downgraded progressive disclosure, the four-layer taxonomy, archive policy, deployment sequence, refresh policy, and local-state claims. It required explicit alternatives for MCP/native/IDE/managed hosts, OCI and marketplace distribution, capability/secret/egress controls, SBOM/VEX, human approvals, kill switches, and alternative rollout models.

Judge: the initial independent judge scored factual accuracy 0.68, citation accuracy 0.57, completeness 0.54, and clarity 0.66, and failed the draft. Remediation narrowed requirements into recommendations, separated SBOM from provenance, corrected transient workspace evidence, added omitted alternatives, and added inline citation anchors.

Re-challenge: the fresh challenger upheld the corrected portable, assurance, local, archive, and release claims; it required exact local locators and narrower SBOM/deployment/currentness wording.

Verification: final artifact review confirmed JSON/schema shape, eight fixed sections, claim-to-reference mappings, dated references, redaction, and no target-code execution. Protected-state baseline at INTAKE: 151 status entries; status digest f9ba6648cc39ad5202abd0ff80d74f08dcaf5f77b79db237f0af2702099e73b7. Existing worktree changes were retained. Active tmux session: csm-deep-research-skill-standards-packaging. No implementation code was changed by this run.
